title: Choose the visual world
question: Porsche Walnut Creek: the roll landed on Light Signature. Keep it, take my pick, adopt an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Light Signature
options.lineage: A modern Porsche at night: four-point LED headlights and the full-width rear light bar
options.thesis: The site introduces the car the way a Porsche introduces itself after dark: by its lights.
options.viewport: Pitch dark. The four-point lights ignite, the live 3D 911 turns to show its tail, and the full-width light bar lights up across the screen as the horizon, carrying WALNUT CREEK lettered like the factory bar, with Build Your Protection right under it.
options.risk: Dark-with-glow is a common AI look. It only escapes that if light stays rationed and every glow is a real lamp color.

raised.raise: Every package ships with a numbered coverage map that is literally true to the 3D car: each number pins to its real panel.
Lamp-only palette lock: every interface color is a real lamp color (DRL white, tail red, indicator amber). No decorative hues or gradients.
One rail: the light bar is the nav, progress and divider. State is carried by line form (lit solid = chosen, dim dashed = available, struck = unavailable), never by extra colors.
Test strips: tint shades and film finishes preview as stepped strips laid across the actual panel before you commit.
PPF coverage drawn as nested cut lines on the car: chosen coverage solid, the other tiers dashed around it, so you see exactly what the next tier adds.
Light is attention: the brightest white on screen belongs only to the thing in focus; everything else sits a step dimmer.

options.label: The Detail Bay
options.lineage: PPF and detailing studios: hexagonal LED grid ceilings mirrored in fresh paint
options.thesis: The protection studio set where protection actually happens: a detail bay under hex lights.
options.viewport: The 911 parked under a hexagonal light ceiling whose reflection slides across the paint as you scroll; the headline sits low over the epoxy floor.
options.risk: Hex-light bays are an Instagram staple for detailers. It's the familiar choice and could read as a detail shop rather than a Porsche Center.

options.label: Ekiben Kiosk
options.lineage: station-platform boxed meals with printed contents maps
options.thesis: Each model and package as a sleeved box whose printed contents map is the index.
options.viewport: A kiosk shelf of model boxes; sliding a band opens one.
options.case: Fuses on clarity (the contents map), but Porsche buyers don't identify with an ekiben kiosk.
options.kept: The numbered coverage map that is true to the car.
options.risk: Reads as food packaging, not a Porsche Center.

options.label: PC-98 Sixteen-Color
options.thesis: The dealership as a dithered 640×400 visual novel.
options.viewport: A dithered sunset with a docked text window.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro novelty fights a luxury buyer and hides the car.
options.kept: Total palette lock: no in-between colors.
options.risk: Pixel art cheapens the paint the studio exists to show.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: glass spectrograms on a viewing box
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one rail; state is line height, dash and doubling.
options.viewport: A charcoal band crossed by needle-thin lines, one doubled.
options.case: Rigorous state system, but abstract; buyers don't read spectrograms.
options.kept: One rail, with state carried by line form instead of color.
options.risk: Too austere to sell a car.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.lineage: photo printing darkrooms under amber safelight
options.thesis: The build develops station by station: compose, expose, develop, fix.
options.viewport: An amber bay where the car emerges in the developer tray.
options.case: Station order and test strips help the studio, but amber murk hides paint color.
options.kept: Test strips that preview tint and finish before committing.
options.risk: Amber wash makes every paint choice look the same.

options.label: Pattern Envelope
options.lineage: home sewing pattern envelopes and cutting tissue
options.thesis: Protection film as a cut pattern: views A/B/C, nested cut lines.
options.viewport: A pattern envelope with the 911 drawn in three views.
options.case: True to how PPF is plotter-cut, but the craft-room look doesn't belong in a Porsche Center.
options.kept: Nested coverage lines: chosen solid, other tiers dashed.

options.label: Luminous Understory
options.thesis: Paths light themselves by proximity; attention is the illumination model.
options.viewport: A dark field where destinations pulse in the distance.
options.case: Loses both axes: fantasy glow has nothing to do with Porsche.
options.kept: Light as attention: the brightest white only on what's in focus.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A luxury car site played straight: big car, black and white, one red accent.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed car hero with the model name and two buttons, a model carousel below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from porsche.com and every dealer template, by design.
